clue.text: Valediction has house enveloped in cloud of dust?

indicators.note: something enveloped in a wrapping sits wholly inside it, so the preceding pieces go inside the dust cloud

parts.note: a puff is a small cloud of smoke or dust
has shortened to 's, as in 'she's got'
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A farewell scene in which a house disappears into a billowing cloud of dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' stands for the contraction 's, as in 'it's got'; the surface makes it a plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Push off! is a brusque way of telling someone to go away, so it serves as a parting word.

clue.text: Fern, no good planted amid meadow-grass

indicators.note: something planted amid a crop is set in the middle of it, so it goes inside

parts.note: Poa is the botanical genus of meadow-grass
NG is the usual abbreviation of no good

explanation.surface: A useless fern stuck in among the grass of a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The ponga is the silver tree fern of New Zealand.

clue.text: Sons, foolish, veering towards supposed revolution

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son or sons
unwise means foolish

explanation.surface: Sons acting foolishly, drifting towards an imagined uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a political uprising, but it is the sun's apparent journey round the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunwise means turning in the direction the sun appears to move, that is, clockwise.

clue.text: English moot halls oddly used as setting for Justice, one subordinate to ayatollah

indicators.note: used oddly means employed in a strange order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
taken as written, part of the fodder
J is the abbreviation for a judge's title, Justice
a means one

explanation.surface: English town halls are strangely turned into courts for a junior Iranian cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: E, MOOT HALLS, J and A are all mixed together; 'setting for' makes them the scene for Justice.
explanation.definitionFit: A hojatoleslam is a Shiite cleric ranking just below an ayatollah.

clue.text: If going uphill, watch the gear you're in

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
to tout is to spy on or keep watch, as racing touts watch horses in training

explanation.surface: Cycling advice: on a climb, keep an eye on which gear you are in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' suggests a bicycle's gears, but it means clothing and equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit-out is a set of clothing or equipment, the outfit someone is wearing or using.

clue.text: Section in iron rod, pointer used by teacher

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the pair of words that follow

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
S is short for section
a cue is the rod used in billiards

explanation.surface: A segment of an iron bar serves as a schoolteacher's pointer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'iron rod' as one object, but iron and rod are separate pieces with the section placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fescue was a small stick or straw a teacher used to point out letters to children learning to read.

clue.text: Five of trumps, lead from player, east, trick capturing king

indicators.note: a piece that captures another holds it inside, so the next item sits within this one
the lead is what goes first, so only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: first letter of player
E is the compass abbreviation for east
to do someone is to cheat or trick them; a do is a swindle
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A card-table report: a player leads, East takes a trick containing the king, and the five of trumps is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a bridge commentary, but 'trick' is a swindle, not a card trick. R goes inside DO.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card games pedro and sancho-pedro, the five of trumps is itself called the pedro and scores points.

clue.text: Essentials fore.g. aromatherapy (12, two words)

parts.note: surface reading: the basic necessities a therapist needs
setter's reading: essentials is short for essential oils, the fragrant plant extracts massaged in during aromatherapy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentials' looks like a general word for basics; it is a clipped form of essential oils, whose older name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile plant oils used in aromatherapy were long called by this older name for essential oils.

clue.text: Badge worn as strip in embarrassing ritual?

indicators.note: something worn is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A badge pinned on for an awkward initiation ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' looks like a badge being displayed; it signals rearrangement. Bags is old slang for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To debag someone is to pull off their trousers as a prank, a traditional ragging ritual at British universities.

clue.text: Obstinate, about to choke

parts.note: re means about, concerning
stive is a dialect verb meaning to stifle or suffocate

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn on the verge of choking.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive originally meant refusing to move forward, as a balky horse does, hence stubborn.

clue.text: Mixed fabric, one found in heraldic borders

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so this piece sits within the borders

parts.note: an orle is a narrow border inset on a heraldic shield
an means one

explanation.surface: A blended cloth, one example of which appears in a coat of arms' edging.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a cloth woven of cotton warp and wool weft, so it is a mixed fabric.

clue.text: Being charitably disposed I put in half capital

indicators.note: to put something in is to insert it, so the letter goes inside the next piece
half keeps only one half of the word's letters

parts.note: the first half of London, the UK capital
taken as written

explanation.surface: A generous mood: I invest in half a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a creature. The Lions Clubs are an international charity organisation whose members are called Lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Lions Club is a lion, someone devoted to charitable service.

clue.text: Cross-country enthusiast transported to Erin always

indicators.note: things transported are carried off and moved about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A lover of cross-country travel is carried off to Ireland for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland, which makes 'transported' look like travel rather than the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An orienteer competes in a sport of running across rough country with map and compass.

clue.text: Martial art: in Japan it is shown in representation of sun

indicators.note: something shown in a frame sits inside it, so these pieces go within the rearranged letters
a representation shows something in another form, so these letters are rearranged into a new pattern

parts.note: J is the international vehicle code for Japan
taken as written
taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Describing a Japanese martial art as being depicted in the form of the rising sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double duty in the surface as a preposition; here it joins 'sun' as letters to be rearranged, with J and IT placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjitsu (or ninjutsu) is the Japanese art of stealth and espionage practised by the ninja.

clue.text: Turn pale as a wild daisy

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: Someone goes as white as a wild daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn pale' reads as one verb phrase; it splits into a noun and an adjective. A gowan is Scots for the daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowan is the Scottish word for a daisy, especially the common wild one.

clue.text: Like a sheath, old make

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
to create is to make

explanation.surface: Describing an antique brand as being sheath-like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' looks like a noun (a brand), but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocrea is a sheathing stipule in botany, so ocreate describes a plant part shaped like or having a sheath.

clue.text: Nancy's alter ego found in a palm tree

parts.note: a and an are both forms of the indefinite article
the ita is the miriti palm of South America

explanation.surface: Nancy's second self turns up hiding in a palm tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy and Anita are both pet forms of the name Ann, so one stands in for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Both girls' names grew from the same root name, Ann or Anne, making each a kind of double of the other.

clue.text: Infamous family headed wild party (or several, strictly)

indicators.note: headed here means having its head cut off, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: the Borgias were a notorious Renaissance Italian family

explanation.surface: A notorious family led a wild party, or several of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed' looks like 'led', but it means beheaded, so BORGIA loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgia is the Latin plural from which orgy comes, so strictly the word names several revels.

clue.text: Hopelessly in love, contrived set-to between the sheets?

indicators.note: something between the sheets lies inside them, so the rearranged letters go within

parts.note: to be between the sheets is to be in bed

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lovers stage a mock fight in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A set-to is a fight; 'contrived' looks like it describes the fight, but it rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Besotted describes someone infatuated to the point of foolishness.

clue.text: One of threesome privy to secret lay beneath plot

definitions.text: One of threesome privy to secret

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath sends the word before it below the word after it, so that one is written second

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
to post is to place or set down, as to lay is

explanation.surface: Someone sworn to secrecy who lay below the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first. The phrase 'between you and me and the bedpost' makes the post a third party to a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'between you and me and the bedpost' treats the post as the third, silent sharer of a confidence.

clue.text: Muscle always reversed deterioration

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the word that follows is written backwards

parts.note: rot is decay

explanation.surface: A muscle that is forever wasting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' sits next to 'always' but applies to the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An evertor is a muscle that turns a part outwards, such as the foot.

clue.text: Cushy bed? Luther's cross!

parts.note: a plum job is a cushy one
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a comfortable bed would make Martin Luther angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Luther' points to the reformer and 'cross' to anger; it is the plant breeder Luther Burbank, and a cross is a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Luther Burbank bred the plumcot, a hybrid of plum and apricot.

clue.text: Devil cleans us — prepares for fishmonger?

indicators.note: to devil food is to work it up with hot seasoning, a culinary roughing-up that signals rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea that the devil scrubs us clean, ready to be sold at the fish counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devil' looks like a noun subject, but it is a cooking verb used as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish are scaled before sale; to unscale a fish is to strip its scales, readying it for the fishmonger's slab.

clue.text: Preparation time, time accepted by what discerning Scotch drinker specifies

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so this letter goes inside the next phrase

parts.note: a whisky purist orders it with no ice
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A whisky drinker's order and the time taken to get ready.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the wordplay both use 'time'; the second one is the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Notice is the warning period given so that people can get ready for something.

clue.text: Minim possibly essential in Pergolesi's terzetti

indicators.note: the essence of something lies inside it, so the letters are found within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A musical note, perhaps a key element in Pergolesi's vocal trios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minim' looks like the half-note and Pergolesi supports the music theme, but a Minim is a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minims are a Catholic order with friars and nuns, so a Minim may be a nun, called sister.

clue.text: Scottish punch to elaborate without work

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: to develop an idea is to elaborate it
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A Scot is told to add detail to a punch without doing any work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link here; OP comes off the end of DEVELOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Devel is a Scots word for a hard blow, so it means a punch.

clue.text: Meat, eastern, obscure to Spenser

parts.note: veal is calf meat
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A list of meat and eastern dishes unknown to the poet Spenser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective meaning unknown, but it is a verb, to cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Veale is Spenser's spelling of veil, to hide or cover from view.

clue.text: Drink without refinement or slight hint of politesse

parts.note: a slight is an insult, as is a slur

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: first letter of politesse

explanation.surface: Drinking crudely, without a trace of good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight hint' reads as one phrase; 'slight' is a noun meaning an insult, and only 'hint of' picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To slurp is to drink noisily, sucking the liquid in a way thought unmannerly.

clue.text: Care for old poet? This is effect on the ears

indicators.note: on the ears means as heard, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: to wreak is to effect or bring about, as in wreaking havoc

explanation.surface: Asking how a poet's work sounds when heard aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb to bring about. 'old poet' marks a word from Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: Reke is Spenser's form of reck, to care or heed.

clue.text: Attitudes are agitating with injection of energy

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the next letter goes within

parts.note: to poss is a dialect word for to agitate washing with a plunger
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Stirred-up attitudes after a dose of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Poses are bodily attitudes, the positions a model or statue takes.

clue.text: Oven controls dailies etc will hold 'alien?

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: daily newspapers and the like are collectively the press
ET, the film's extraterrestrial, is the crossword alien

explanation.surface: Domestic cleaners and their oven settings, with a dropped-aitch 'alien' thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dailies' suggests cleaning ladies near an oven, but they are newspapers. The apostrophe hints at a Cockney 'h' dropped from 'halien'.
explanation.definitionFit: Presets are settings fixed in advance, such as programmed temperatures on a cooker.

clue.text: Swain? The old man maybe collars me

indicators.note: a collar goes round the neck, so the first piece wraps round the next

parts.note: an old man is an adult male kangaroo, and roo is short for kangaroo
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young suitor gets grabbed by the scruff by the girl's father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old man' looks like a father, but in Australia an old man is a big male kangaroo; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, after Shakespeare's lover, is a byword for an ardent suitor, which is what a swain is.

clue.text: Is carping best confined to fools?

indicators.note: something confined is shut inside, so the first piece sits within the second

parts.note: nits are idiots
the pick of a bunch is the best

explanation.surface: Asking whether fault-finding is best left to idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over trivial details, which is what carping means.

clue.text: Unusual collars round part of building, source of free energy (9, two words)

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the next piece
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an out-of-the-ordinary order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an el (or ell) is a wing of a building at right angles to the main part

explanation.surface: Odd neckwear wrapped round a section of a building, giving free power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collars' looks like a verb meaning seizes; it is the set of letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar cell turns sunlight, which costs nothing, into electricity.

clue.text: Dotty 'hat' prompting some covert remarks

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters run on inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A spotty hat sets off whispered asides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' seems to mean crazy, but it means made of dots.
explanation.definitionFit: A trema is the diaeresis, two dots set over a letter like a little cap.

clue.text: Physician challenging church authority uses art deftly

indicators.note: doing something deftly suggests skilful handling, so the letters are nimbly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor who defies the Church does so with skill and flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Erastus, a sixteenth-century Swiss physician and theologian, argued that the state, not the church, should punish sins.
